belongs_to: Printed answer under book 'Page No. 30' to "Use the power line for 7 to answer the following questions." (Power Lines, section 2.3): the completed power line for 7 with the eight printed equations beside it
description: A vertical power line (a vertical black line with 12 short horizontal ticks crossing it, equally spaced, the line running a little above the top tick and a little below the bottom tick). Three columns, read top to bottom. LEFT column (exponent labels, one at the left end of each tick): 7^7, 7^6, 7^5, 7^4, 7^3, 7^2, 7^1, 7^0, 7^-1, 7^-2, 7^-3, 7^-4. MIDDLE column (value written to the right of each tick, same order, plain digits with no commas): 823543, 117649, 16807, 2401, 343, 49, 7, 1, then the stacked fractions 1/7, 1/49, 1/343, 1/2401. RIGHT column (not tied to any tick, no arrows or connectors; eight printed equations, in this order top to bottom): (1) 2,401 × 49 = 7^6; (2) 49^3 = 7^6; (3) 343 × 2,401 = 7^7; (4) 16,807 / 49 = 7^3 (stacked fraction); (5) 7 / 343 = 7^-2 (stacked fraction); (6) 16,807 / 8,23,543 = 7^-2 (stacked fraction); (7) 1,17,649 × (1/343) = 7^3; (8) (1/343) × (1/343) = 7^-6. The equations use Indian-style commas (1,17,649 and 8,23,543) while the middle column has none. No colour, shading, highlight, circle or arrow anywhere; all black on white. The same power line (values given, answers blank) is printed in the chapter on book page 30 (pdf page 12) for the question.

belongs_to: Book 'Page No. 32' question: "The number line below shows the distance between the Sun and Saturn (1.4335 × 10^12 m). On the number line below, mark the relative position of the Earth. The distance between the Sun and the Earth is 1.496 × 10^11 m." (reprinted in the answer part)
description: A blank horizontal number line, no scale numbers. A horizontal black line with exactly two vertical end-ticks (each tick crosses the line, extending above and below it): the left tick at the very left end of the line with the label 'Sun' under it, and the right tick about 90 percent of the way along with the label 'Saturn' under it. The line continues a little past the Saturn tick (about one-tenth of the Sun-Saturn length) and ends with no tick. There are no other ticks, no Earth mark, no arrows, no numbers and no colour. This is the question's figure; the student has to mark the Earth on it.

belongs_to: Printed answer ('Ans:') to the book 'Page No. 32' question: mark the relative position of the Earth on the Sun-Saturn number line
description: The same horizontal black line as the question figure, now divided by vertical ticks into 10 equal parts: 11 ticks in all (each tick crosses the line, above and below it), counted from the left as tick 0 to tick 10. Tick 0 (the left end of the line) is labelled 'Sun'; tick 1 (one interval to the right of the Sun) is labelled 'Earth'; ticks 2 to 9 (8 ticks) are unlabelled; tick 10 is labelled 'Saturn'. The line runs about one interval past the Saturn tick and ends with no tick. So the Earth sits at one tenth of the Sun-Saturn length (1.496 × 10^11 is about 1/10 of 1.4335 × 10^12). No numbers on the ticks, no arrows, no colour, no shading; the only difference from the question figure is the 9 added ticks and the 'Earth' label.
